A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-VLA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary sections support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original robot-manipulation experiments under low illumination and motion blur, together with ablations, reconstruction comparisons, and supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results using a π0.5 backbone and an image-augmentation control.

M1.justification: The recent-count representation, overlay fusion, hierarchical event adapter, and staged training remain unchanged. The π0.5 experiment tests another backbone without documenting a new method component or adaptation.

E1.justification: Both retain the 724-episode dataset, Pick-Place/Sorting/Stacking tasks, and existing illumination and motion-blur coverage. The new experiments reuse Pick-Place at 75–20 lux; synthetic training augmentation changes preprocessing rather than task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an augmented-image policy comparator in Table S10 and evaluates image-only π0.5 against its event-adapter variant in Table S8. The original enhancement, reconstruction, and image-only comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce π0.5 evaluation and an augmentation control applying gamma reduction of 1.1–2.8 and directional blur of 3–15 pixels to 80% of training data. Both new tables specify 20 trials. The existing evaluation protocol is retained.

E4.justification: New Sections 8.3 and 10.1 test whether benefits transfer to another VLA backbone and whether aggressive image augmentation can substitute for event sensing. These are targeted additions to the retained windowing, training, representation, dropout, and failure analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point success rates without seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables' 20-trial captions specify evaluation sample sizes; they do not establish a new repeated-run uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table S8 reports average success of 55.8% for image-only π0.5 and 95.0% with the event adapter. New Table S10 reports 47.9%, 51.7%, and 93.3% for image-only, augmented-image, and event-adapter policies. These supplement the unchanged original results rather than replace them.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same event, windowing, representation, overlay, and adapter-fusion definitions. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework, dataset, fusion, and robustness contributions and headline results. The abstract's exposure-proxy wording clarifies the blur description without establishing a different core claim.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets the π0.5 results as evidence of transfer across architectures and the insufficiency of capacity scaling alone. It interprets the augmentation results as supporting event sensing beyond software augmentation. Existing color, occlusion, passive-perception, and generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit augmentation ranges and application frequency, and adds a schematic detailing event and action buffering. Existing network dimensions, training schedules, hardware, and code/data access statements are retained; π0.5-specific implementation details remain sparse.

R1.justification: The same 68 referenced works and related-work positioning are retained. π0.5 was already cited in v1; its new evaluation does not redefine the paper's novelty claims. Removed bibliography back-references are formatting changes.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and typo corrections, revises author affiliation/contribution notes, adds acknowledgments, and inserts two supplementary subsections. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the execution schematic in Figure 3 and new Tables S8 and S10. Existing figures and tables are retained with relocation and renumbering. Page dimensions, margins, and citation styling change, while the underlying single-column design remains.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked a second-backbone test and an aggressive training-augmentation control. V2 adds both, providing useful evidence about architecture dependence and the benefit of event sensing beyond augmentation. The execution schematic also improves explanation. These are limited gains: the new tests remain within existing Pick-Place illumination settings, with sparse π0.5-specific implementation details and no uncertainty estimates.
